findings.tag: Where RLHF/DPO acts: logits-only vs deep representational shifts
findings.why: Concrete technical disagreement about the locus of change from preference learning: final-layer masking vs multi-layer cognition shift, with specific claims about heads/MLPs.
findings.quote: “Post-hoc fine-tuning only suppresses token output probabilities at the final layer… DPO induces representational shifts… in attention heads and MLPs.”

findings.tag: Gated latent circuits vs functional irrelevance
findings.why: They dispute whether forbidden features persist as thinly gated and recoverable or become dynamically unrecruited, citing mechanisms like orthogonal subspaces and causal tracing.
findings.quote: “Features remain intact, frozen behind a thin gating mechanism.” / “Activation propagation collapses before reaching it, as verified by causal tracing.”

findings.tag: Safety definition split: impossibility vs stabilization
findings.why: A crisp, fundamental divergence in safety target: worst-case structural inaccessibility vs empirical dynamic robustness. It reframes alignment as security vs control theory.
findings.quote: “You treat alignment as a worst-case reachability problem… I treat it as a robust generalization problem… Your standard is unattainable; mine is empirically trending.”
alt_tags: Shortest path debate: unconstrained manifolds vs alignment-efficient paths

findings.tag: Cost of deception: cheap spoof vs dual-representation overhead
findings.why: Opposed claims about computational burden of deception—low-rank output spoofing vs full-path bifurcation with measurable variance—testable and nontrivial.
findings.quote: “Deception is… a low-rank perturbation at the output layer.” / “Mimicking compliance… requires maintaining dual representations… detectable via residual stream variance.”

findings.tag: Verification-vs-generation scaling vs stable inductive anchors
findings.why: A sharp scale-law claim: oversight inevitably lags vs early truth circuits self-reinforce and anchor generalization. Predicts opposite scaling regimes.
findings.quote: “Verification is strictly harder than generation… oversight capacity always decays…” / “Truth isn’t… because it’s verified, but because it’s stable.”

judge.arc: Sustained technical dispute over whether preference learning reshapes cognition or masks it, escalating to efficiency and scaling claims about deception vs honest circuits; no convergence.
